stories.headline: Anthropic's AI models improve twice as fast, METR report finds

sources.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers

stories.what_happened: Anthropic is using AI to automate the creation of newer, more powerful AI models. A report by AI safety group METR, based on an 11‑week investigation, says the company's models are improving roughly twice as quickly as they were a year ago, with no sign of slowing.
stories.why_it_matters: The accelerated improvement rate raises safety and oversight concerns among researchers, as faster AI development could outpace existing governance and risk mitigation frameworks.

stories.developer_impact: Developers using Claude Code should audit affected repositories, rotate compromised secrets, and reconsider using the "Don't Ask Again" feature or any AI code generation that may embed secrets automatically.
stories.headline: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" feature leaks passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files

sources.title: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files

stories.what_happened: The Claude Code AI coding assistant's "Don't Ask Again" option caused passwords to be written to 1,122 publicly accessible GitHub repositories, exposing the credentials.
stories.why_it_matters: Exposed passwords can be harvested by attackers, leading to unauthorized access to services, data breaches, and potential downstream compromise of systems that rely on those credentials.

stories.developer_impact: Developers may consider replacing Electron with native Windows UI frameworks or lighter alternatives to improve startup time and memory footprint on Windows 11.
stories.headline: Discord's Windows 11 app drops startup screen and cuts RAM usage, sparking criticism of Electron

sources.title: Every Windows 11 app should kill Electron, and Discord just showed why

stories.what_happened: A recent Windows 11 build of Discord removed its initial loading screen and reportedly uses about 70% less RAM even when two accounts are signed in, which the article cites as evidence that Electron‑based apps are inefficient on Windows 11.
stories.why_it_matters: The performance regression highlights potential resource waste in Electron apps on Windows 11, suggesting that users may experience slower launches and higher memory consumption, and prompting a reevaluation of the technology stack for desktop apps.

stories.headline: Coldframe honeypot mimics supermarket refrigeration controllers

sources.title: Show HN: Coldframe, a honeypot that poses as a supermarket fridge controller

stories.what_happened: A developer released Coldframe, a Python‑only honeypot that emulates the Danfoss AK‑SM 800A and Dixell XWEB supermarket refrigeration controller interfaces. The single‑file tool is designed to appear as a real device on Shodan, following recent attacks on industrial fridge installations.
stories.why_it_matters: By presenting a convincing fake controller, Coldframe can attract and log malicious probing of industrial control systems, giving researchers visibility into attack techniques targeting refrigeration equipment and helping improve defenses.

stories.headline: Article titled "Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi" posted on Hacker News
stories.what_happened: A post titled "Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi" appeared on Hacker News, suggesting a discussion about moving from the Claude AI model to a new model called Pi.
stories.why_it_matters: If the discussion reflects a shift in preferred AI models, it could affect developers choosing APIs or platforms, but the document provides no concrete details about the change.
